_provenance.notes: Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) was established by the 1996 Magnuson-Stevens Act reauthorization. EFH includes all waters and substrates necessary for fish spawning, breeding, feeding, and growth to maturity. In Alaska, EFH designations cover most of the continental shelf and nearshore waters. Habitat Areas of Particular Concern (HAPC) are the most sensitive and specifically protected subsets of EFH.

alaska_efh_designations.description: Major EFH and HAPC designations relevant to Alaska fisheries

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Soft bottom continental shelf (0-500m) from SEAK to BSAI
efh_areas.critical_habitat: Near-bottom structure — sponge beds, coral gardens along shelf edge
hapc: Glass sponge reefs — GOA shelf edge

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Eastern Bering Sea shelf (50-300m), particularly cold pool edge
threats: Bottom trawling on juvenile nursery habitat

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Shallow shelf (10-200m) rocky and soft bottom; nearshore eelgrass for juveniles
efh_areas.critical_habitat: PWS shallow bays (Chiniak Bay, Kachemak Bay) for juvenile nursery
threats: Climate warming reducing cold juvenile habitat

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Spawning: clean gravel stream substrate; Rearing: riparian freshwater; Ocean: 0-200m continental shelf
efh_areas.critical_habitat: Designated critical habitat: Major river systems under ESA for listed stocks

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Deep water (200-1500m) rocky slope and shelf edge; fjords for spawning
efh_areas.critical_habitat: Lynn Canal, Chatham Strait (SEAK) — known spawning aggregation areas
threats: Bottom trawling (longline managed but trawl bycatch)

efh_areas.primary_habitat: Sandy/muddy bottom 0-200m; historically tied to cold pool (snow crab); rocky bottom for BBRKC
efh_areas.critical_habitat: Pribilof Islands shallow shelf — key BBRKC habitat
threats: Bottom trawling on crab nursery habitat
Ocean acidification affecting juvenile shell formation

coral_sponge_hapc.description: Alaska Habitat Areas of Particular Concern — Coral and Sponge Ecosystems
coral_sponge_hapc.notes: The Aleutian Islands coral and sponge gardens are among the most biologically diverse deep-sea ecosystems in the world. They were heavily damaged by bottom trawling before restrictions were implemented in 2006.
coral_sponge_hapc.age_of_coral_colonies: Some Aleutian bamboo corals are estimated at 1,800-3,000 years old
